claims.text: The target material is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding are governed by formation and evolution of a nanocrystalline surface layer.
The nanocrystalline surface layer can be observed and characterized using in-situ TEM or SEM.
Varying deposition parameters provides controlled changes in coating grain size and composition.
The proposed operating regime is sliding above 500 °C.
Formation and evolution of the nanocrystalline surface layer enhance wear resistance.
Formation and evolution of the nanocrystalline surface layer reduce microscopic deformation.
Decreasing coating grain size increases wear resistance under the stated regime.
Decreasing coating grain size reduces microscopic deformation under the stated regime.
An optimized composition increases wear resistance and reduces microscopic deformation.
The baseline coating has a grain size of 100 nm and composition Fe30Ni30Cr20Co10Cu10 in atomic percent.
The predictions are intended to hold for grain sizes below 50 nm.
The predictions are intended to hold for composition variations within 10% of the baseline composition.
Absence of a correlation between nanocrystalline-layer evolution and wear resistance or microscopic deformation would falsify the hypothesis.
